deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy the resource. A policy should require destruction protection (for example, PREVENT) to reduce accidental or malicious deletion of critical infrastructure.

description.description: A human-readable description of the resource.
description.rationale: Human-readable description used for documentation only. It does not affect the security posture of the resource.

forwarding_rules.description:
A list of references to the forwarding rules to which this service extension is attached.
At least one forwarding rule is required. Only one LbEdgeExtension resource can be associated with a forwarding rule.
forwarding_rules.rationale: References existing forwarding rule resources. Platform policy should not constrain which forwarding rules a team chooses to attach.

labels.description:
Set of labels associated with the LbEdgeExtension resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Metadata used for organization and resource management. Labels do not affect security behaviour.

load_balancing_scheme.description: All forwarding rules referenced by this extension must share the same load balancing scheme. Possible values: ["EXTERNAL_MANAGED"]
load_balancing_scheme.rationale: Specifies the load balancing architecture. This is a functional deployment choice rather than a generic security control, and platform policy should not enforce one architecture over another.

location.description: The location of the edge extension
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: Name of the LbEdgeExtension resource in the following format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/lbEdgeExtensions/{lbEdgeExtensions}
name.rationale: Resource identifier only. Platform policy should not constrain resource names.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project containing the resource. Platform policy should not constrain project identifiers.

extension_chains.description:
A set of ordered extension chains that contain the match conditions and extensions to execute.
Match conditions for each extension chain are evaluated in sequence for a given request.
The first extension chain that has a condition that matches the request is executed.
Any subsequent extension chains do not execute. Limited to 5 extension chains per resource.

extension_chains.name.description:
The name for this extension chain. The name is logged as part of the HTTP request logs.
The name must conform with RFC-1034, is restricted to lower-cased letters, numbers and hyphens,
and can have a maximum length of 63 characters. Additionally, the first character must be a letter
and the last character must be a letter or a number.
extension_chains.name.rationale: Name of the extension chain used for identification and logging. It is an identifier and does not affect security.

extension_chains.extensions.description:
A set of extensions to execute for the matching request.
At least one extension is required. Up to 3 extensions can be defined for each extension chain for
LbTrafficExtension resource. LbRouteExtension chains are limited to 1 extension per extension chain.

extension_chains.extensions.fail_open.description:
Determines how the proxy behaves if the call to the extension fails or times out.
When set to TRUE, request or response processing continues without error.
Any subsequent extensions in the extension chain are also executed.
When set to FALSE: * If response headers have not been delivered to the downstream client,
a generic 500 error is returned to the client. The error response can be tailored by
configuring a custom error response in the load balancer.
extension_chains.extensions.fail_open.rationale: Controls gateway behaviour when the extension fails. A policy should require fail-closed (false) so requests are not processed when security extensions are unavailable.

extension_chains.extensions.forward_head.description:
List of the HTTP headers to forward to the extension (from the client or backend).
If omitted, all headers are sent. Each element is a string indicating the header name.
extension_chains.extensions.forward_head.rationale: Controls which HTTP headers are forwarded to the extension. A policy should restrict forwarded headers to only those required, reducing unnecessary exposure of sensitive information.

extension_chains.extensions.name.description:
The name for this extension. The name is logged as part of the HTTP request logs.
The name must conform with RFC-1034, is restricted to lower-cased letters, numbers and hyphens,
and can have a maximum length of 63 characters. Additionally, the first character must be a letter
and the last a letter or a number.
extension_chains.extensions.name.rationale: Identifier for the extension. Platform policy should not constrain resource names.

extension_chains.extensions.service.description:
The reference to the service that runs the extension.

* To configure a callout extension, service must be a fully-qualified reference to a backend service.
* To configure a plugin extension, service must be a reference to a WasmPlugin resource.
extension_chains.extensions.service.rationale: References an existing backend service or WasmPlugin resource. It is a pointer to another resource, and platform policy should not dictate which service is used.

extension_chains.extensions.supported_ev.description:
A set of events during request or response processing for which this extension is called.
This field is required for the LbEdgeExtension resource and only supports the value 'REQUEST_HEADERS'.
extension_chains.extensions.supported_ev.rationale: Specifies which request-processing events invoke the extension. This is functional behaviour rather than a generic security control.

extension_chains.match_condition.description: Conditions under which this chain is invoked for a request.

extension_chains.match_condition.cel_exp.description: A Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that is used to match requests for which the extension chain is executed.
extension_chains.match_condition.cel_exp.rationale: Defines request matching using a CEL expression. It is a free-form policy expression that cannot be generically constrained by a platform security policy.
